hero.headline: Global stock markets fall as tech shares slide and Middle East conflict escalates
hero.body:
Stock markets across Asia and Europe declined sharply on Monday following a steep sell-off in US technology stocks and rising concerns about valuations in the artificial intelligence sector. The sell-off was compounded by renewed military conflict between Iran and Israel, which sent oil prices surging.

In Asia, losses were particularly severe. South Korea's Kospi index slumped nearly 9% at one point, forcing trading to be briefly suspended. Chip manufacturers led the decline, with Samsung Electronics dropping 9% and SK Hynix falling 6%. Japan's Nikkei 225 index fell 3%, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng dropped 1.5%.

European markets also opened lower. London's FTSE 100 fell 0.4%, with travel and aerospace companies including British Airways parent IAG and jet engine maker Rolls-Royce among the biggest losers. Oil companies BP and Shell bucked the trend with gains. Stock markets in Germany, France and Spain also declined. The pan-European Stoxx 600 index fell nearly 0.9%, with semiconductor firms and technology companies suffering sharp losses. Chip equipment maker ASML fell 3.2%, while German tech firm Aixtron dropped nearly 6% and Finland's Nokia fell 5%.

The technology sector retreat followed a prolonged rally in artificial intelligence stocks that had driven valuations to elevated levels. Investors are increasingly concerned about how major technology companies will fund their substantial capital expenditure plans, particularly if interest rates rise. Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, noted that markets are now pricing in a greater likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate increase this year. She stated: "The demand is voracious right now, but there is concern that assets being invested in today, at a time when the technology is so expensive, could become obsolete further down the road."

Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo, said the market was becoming more selective about AI investments. "Investors now want clearer proof of earnings delivery, monetisation, capex discipline and funding returns," Chanana said. "This looks more like a positioning reset than a regime break. The AI story is not over, but easy AI enthusiasm may be."

Oil prices jumped nearly 5% to $97.60 per barrel after Iran and Israel exchanged direct strikes. The conflict has heightened concerns about potential disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping channel through which about a fifth of the world's oil and gas normally flows. Analysts warned that escalation could prevent the waterway's reopening and prolong inflationary pressures on the global economy.

The combination of falling technology valuations and rising oil costs created significant turbulence across global financial markets. US markets were expected to open lower on Monday, continuing the decline that ended nine weeks of consecutive gains for the broader S&P 500, which dropped 2% on a weekly basis.

cards.headline: Earthquake in Philippines Kills at Least 15
cards.teaser: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck off the coast of the Philippines, triggering tsunami warnings and causing at least 15 deaths.
cards.body:
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck the southern Philippines on Monday, killing at least 19 people and injuring more than 200 others. The powerful quake caused buildings to collapse across multiple areas and generated a 3-foot tsunami that reached nearby coasts.

Rescue operations were underway as authorities assessed the damage. Officials warned residents to avoid entering damaged buildings and structures due to the risk of aftershocks following the initial tremor.

cards.body:
South Korea's Kospi index fell 8% as investors unwound positions in technology stocks that had surged on AI optimism. The sell-off followed a sharp decline in US tech stocks the previous week, as markets reassessed whether companies at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom could justify their substantial spending plans.

The pullback reflects broader concerns about valuations across Asia's tech sector. Foreign investors have withdrawn billions from Korean stocks this year, reversing the gains that had been fueled by expectations about South Korea's role in the global AI supply chain. The decline contributed to losses in stock markets across Asia and Europe.

cards.headline: Atlantic ocean current system shows signs of approaching tipping point
cards.body:
New research has significantly increased concerns that the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, or AMOC, is heading toward a critical collapse. Scientists say the findings are "very concerning" because a breakdown of this major ocean system would have catastrophic consequences for Europe, Africa, and the Americas.

The AMOC is already at its weakest point in 1,600 years due to climate change. It functions like a conveyor belt, carrying warm tropical water north to Europe and the Arctic, where it cools and sinks to form a deep return current. The system plays a crucial role in regulating global climate patterns and influences everything from weather systems to fish populations across multiple continents.

A mysterious cold blob in the North Atlantic has served as a visible sign of the circulation's decline. Scientists have also detected hidden warming deep beneath the Atlantic surface, a pattern consistent with a weakening current system.

The new analysis, published in Science Advances, combined real-world ocean observations with climate models to identify which predictions are most reliable. Previous climate models produced widely varying results, ranging from no further slowdown by 2100 to a 65% deceleration. By narrowing down to the most realistic models, researchers found an estimated slowdown of 42% to 58% by 2100, a level almost certain to trigger collapse.

Dr Valentin Portmann, who led the research, stated: "We found that the AMOC is going to decline more than expected compared to the average of all climate models. This means we have an AMOC that is closer to a tipping point."

Professor Stefan Rahmstorf from the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research said: "This is an important and very concerning result. It shows that the pessimistic models, which show a strong weakening of the AMOC by 2100, are, unfortunately, the realistic ones."

Rahmstorf, who has studied the AMOC for 35 years, expressed growing concern about the timeline. He warned that "we may well pass that AMOC shutdown tipping point, where it becomes inevitable, in the middle of this century, which is quite close." He previously argued the risk was too high even when estimated at 5%, but now believes it exceeds 50%.

The AMOC is slowing because Arctic air temperatures are rising rapidly due to global heating. Warmer ocean water is less dense and sinks more slowly, while increased rainfall freshens surface waters, creating a feedback loop that further slows the circulation.

A collapse would shift tropical rainfall patterns that billions of people depend on for food production, plunge Western Europe into extreme cold winters and severe droughts, and add 50 to 100 centimeters to rising sea levels around the Atlantic.

Rahmstorf noted that the slowdown could be even more severe than current predictions because climate models do not account for additional freshwater from melting Greenland ice.

cards.headline: Armenia's Pro-West Government Wins Election
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan secured re-election in Armenia despite pressure from Moscow, winning nearly 50% of the vote.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's Civil Contract Party secured nearly 50% of the vote in parliamentary elections, winning a decisive mandate despite opposition from Moscow. The result strengthens Armenia's strategic shift away from its traditional Russian alliance toward closer ties with Europe and the West.

The election victory confirms Pashinyan's drive to deepen integration with European institutions and advance regional peace negotiations. The opposition Strong Armenia alliance, backed by a Russian-Armenian billionaire, captured 25% of parliamentary seats but failed to challenge the ruling party's dominance.

cards.headline: Six people stabbed at Penn Station in New York City, suspect in custody
cards.body:
Six people were injured in a stabbing attack at Penn Station in New York City, with a suspect now in police custody. The incident occurred at one of the busiest transportation hubs in the United States, which serves hundreds of thousands of commuters daily through Amtrak, Long Island Rail Road, and subway lines.

The attack took place during morning hours when the station typically experiences heavy commuter traffic. Emergency responders transported all the injured victims for medical treatment. Police apprehended a suspect following the incident.

Penn Station serves as a critical transit point in Manhattan, connecting commuters from across the New York metropolitan area and the Northeast corridor. The facility handles substantial passenger volume on a daily basis, making it one of the most heavily trafficked transportation centers in North America.

The stabbing adds to ongoing concerns about public safety in New York City's transit system. Violence in subway stations and major transit hubs has become a recurring issue in recent years, prompting authorities to implement increased security measures and expand police presence throughout the network. Penn Station itself has been the subject of various safety initiatives designed to protect the large numbers of passengers who pass through the facility each day.

Details about what prompted the attack remain unclear. Authorities have not disclosed information regarding the motivation behind the stabbing or provided updates on the medical condition of the injured victims. The investigation was ongoing at the scene following the incident.

Despite the attack, transit operations continued with minimal disruption. Police maintained their presence at the station as they gathered evidence and conducted interviews related to the incident.

The stabbing underscores the safety challenges facing New York City's transportation network. Penn Station, which serves as a gateway for hundreds of thousands of daily passengers, has faced repeated security concerns over the years. The combination of high foot traffic, multiple entry and exit points, and constant passenger flow creates significant challenges for maintaining security at the facility.

City officials have worked to address safety concerns through various means, including deploying additional officers at major transit hubs and implementing surveillance upgrades. However, incidents continue to occur despite these efforts.

The New York Police Department did not immediately release comprehensive details about the incident, including the identities of those involved or specific circumstances that led to the attack. Standard procedures called for detectives to interview witnesses and review security footage from the station.

Commuters and transit officials have expressed ongoing concern about personal safety while using the city's transportation system. The incident at Penn Station, one of the region's largest transit centers, highlights the persistent security challenges facing the New York area.

cards.headline: Peru Election Result Remains Close as Counting Continues
cards.teaser: Right-wing candidate Keiko Fujimori and left-wing candidate Roberto Sánchez remain in a tight race as vote counting continues in Peru.
cards.body:
Peru's presidential runoff between right-wing candidate Keiko Fujimori and left-wing congressman Roberto Sánchez has captured voter attention amid widespread concerns about rising crime and political instability. Fujimori, daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, won 17% in the first round, while Sánchez secured 12%, narrowly surpassing ultra-conservative Rafael López Aliaga.

The election represents a polarized left-right contest similar to Peru's 2021 presidential race. Voters face a choice between competing visions as the country struggles with corruption scandals and chronic political turmoil. Peru has seen nine presidents in a decade, reflecting deep institutional challenges and voter dissatisfaction with government performance.

cards.headline: Malawi Repatriates Citizens From South Africa
cards.teaser: Malawi is transporting citizens out of South Africa following reports of violence against migrants and rising xenophobia concerns.
cards.body:
Malawi is among several African nations repatriating their citizens from South Africa following escalating xenophobic violence against migrants. The government has organized transportation to bring Malawians home as tensions in the country intensify.

The repatriations come as South Africa experiences renewed anti-immigrant sentiment. A campaign group called March & March has been leading protests demanding illegal immigrants leave the country by June 30. African migrants report living in extreme fear, noting that legal status offers little protection amid the hostile climate and organized rallies against immigration.

cards.headline: Pope and Spanish Prime Minister Unite in Opposition to Trump
cards.teaser: Pope Leo XIV met with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, with both leaders having recently clashed with President Trump.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez met on Monday, bringing together two leaders who have both publicly opposed President Trump in recent weeks. The meeting highlighted their shared willingness to challenge US policy, though their underlying motivations may differ.

The Pope and Sánchez represent different perspectives, with one leading the Catholic Church and the other identifying as an atheist. Despite their philosophical differences, both have emerged as critics of Trump administration policies, creating an unusual alliance across religious and political lines.

cards.headline: Controversy Over Mexico World Cup Jerseys
cards.teaser: Mexicans expressed outrage after viral videos claimed Adidas exploited Indigenous women to sew World Cup jerseys.
cards.body:
Viral videos sparked outrage in Mexico with allegations that Adidas exploited Indigenous women producing World Cup jerseys. The claims prompted journalists to travel to mountain communities to investigate directly with the artisans involved in manufacturing the kits.

The central question dividing observers is whether the involvement of Indigenous craftswomen constitutes fair artisanal partnership or labor exploitation. The dispute reflects broader concerns about how multinational brands work with traditional communities and whether they fairly compensate artisans for their work and cultural knowledge.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall on Tech Decline and Middle East Tensions
cards.teaser: Markets in Europe and Asia dropped as technology stocks plunged and renewed attacks between Iran and Israel pushed oil prices higher.
cards.body:
Global stock markets in Asia and Europe fell on Monday following a sharp sell-off in US technology stocks the previous week. Investors grew concerned about major tech firms driving the artificial intelligence boom and their ability to finance substantial spending commitments.

Oil prices climbed as Iran and Israel exchanged military strikes, reigniting Middle East tensions and dimming prospects for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The combination of tech sector weakness and renewed geopolitical conflict created turbulence across global markets.

cards.headline: Remote work linked to increased social isolation and anxiety in new study
cards.teaser: Research finds people working remotely experience higher levels of social isolation, anxiety, and sadness compared to office workers.
cards.body:
A new study has found that people working in remote jobs experience greater social isolation, anxiety, and sadness compared to those not working remotely. The research highlights mental health challenges associated with working from home, despite its popularity among employees.

Researchers say the solution is not simply demanding everyone return to the office. The findings suggest a more nuanced approach is needed to address the social and emotional impacts of remote work while preserving flexibility that many workers value.

cards.headline: Whales entering San Francisco Bay as climate shifts, prompting new ship alert system
cards.teaser: Changing climate patterns are bringing whales into San Francisco Bay, where ship strikes have killed them, leading to new camera technology to prevent collisions.
cards.body:
Climate change is shifting whale migration patterns and feeding grounds, drawing the marine mammals into San Francisco Bay in increasing numbers. Ship strikes have proven deadly for these whales, creating a serious safety concern for both the animals and vessel traffic in the bay.

In response, a new camera system has been deployed to detect whales and alert ships and ferries to their presence. The technology enables vessel operators to adjust course in real time, helping reduce the risk of collisions and protect the whales navigating bay waters.

cards.headline: Political and geographic sorting in US driven by multiple factors beyond ideology
cards.teaser: Research shows Americans are sorting themselves by geography based on politics, taxes, and safety concerns, not just political views alone.
cards.body:
Recent research indicates that the division between red states and blue states reflects more than political preferences. People are making location decisions based on a combination of factors including taxes, safety, and other quality of life considerations, with politics serving as one element among many.

The study suggests that ideological sorting is happening, but it is driven by a complex set of priorities rather than partisan identity alone. Economic considerations and public safety concerns play significant roles in where Americans choose to live, contributing to the geographic clustering of like-minded populations.

cards.headline: FDA-approved vibrating belt may slow bone density loss in older adults
cards.teaser: More than 40 million Americans aged 50 and older have low bone density, and a new wearable vibration device offers a potential treatment option.
cards.body:
More than 40 million Americans aged 50 and older have osteopenia, a condition characterized by low bone density that increases fracture risk. An FDA-approved wearable vibration device offers women a new option for addressing this widespread health concern.

The vibrating belt technology provides a non-pharmaceutical approach to slowing bone density loss, expanding the treatment toolkit available to older adults managing osteopenia.

cards.headline: Arthur Miller revival wins big at Tony Awards as John Lithgow and Lesley Manville take top acting honors
cards.teaser: A revival of Death of a Salesman earned six awards at the Tony Awards ceremony, with veteran actors taking home lead performance prizes.
cards.body:
A revival of Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman emerged as the biggest winner at the Tony Awards, collecting six awards throughout the night. The production's success highlighted renewed interest in classic American theater.

John Lithgow and Lesley Manville led the acting winners, taking home top honors for their performances. The awards ceremony recognized achievements across Broadway productions during the season.

cards.headline: Magnitude 7.8 earthquake in southern Philippines kills at least 19
cards.teaser: A powerful earthquake struck the southern Philippines, triggering small tsunami waves across the region and causing significant casualties.
cards.body:
A powerful 7.8 magnitude earthquake struck southern Philippines early Monday, killing at least 19 people and injuring more than 200 others. The offshore quake caused buildings to collapse across the region and generated a 3-foot tsunami that reached nearby coasts in the Philippines, Indonesia, and Japan.

Rescue operations were underway as authorities warned residents to avoid damaged buildings due to the threat of aftershocks. The region, located along the Pacific Ring of Fire, experiences frequent seismic activity that makes it vulnerable to earthquakes and volcanic events.

cards.headline: Airlines face $100 billion additional fuel costs as Iran conflict disrupts supplies
cards.teaser: Global airlines have slashed profit forecasts for 2026 as jet fuel costs surge due to the energy shock from the Iran conflict.
cards.body:
The global airline industry is confronting an additional $100 billion in jet fuel expenses this year due to the energy crisis stemming from the Iran conflict. International Air Transport Association officials addressed the financial strain at the organization's 82nd Annual General Meeting, warning that carriers worldwide face significant margin pressure.

Airlines have already begun cutting their 2026 profit forecasts in response to the fuel shock. The increased operating costs are expected to lead to inevitable rises in airfare prices as carriers seek to offset the unprecedented spike in energy expenses. Industry analysts suggest the fuel crisis represents one of the most severe cost pressures airlines have faced in recent years.

cards.headline: Europe's economic recovery stalls as war in Iran drives prolonged inflation
cards.teaser: Signs point to an extended period of higher prices and slower growth across Europe rather than the quick economic shock that some analysts had anticipated.
cards.body:
Middle East tensions are weighing on Europe's economic outlook. Oil prices have surged as the Iran conflict intensifies, threatening to sustain elevated inflation across the continent and constrain growth. Global stock markets have also declined amid the geopolitical uncertainty and selling pressure in technology shares.

Energy-dependent European economies face particular vulnerability to sustained oil price increases. Policymakers had expected stronger growth momentum, but the persistent Middle East conflict now points toward a prolonged period of higher prices and slower expansion rather than a brief economic disruption.

cards.headline: AI chip concentration in Asian indices forces funds to sell top-performing stocks
cards.teaser: Investment funds have been compelled to sell shares of major semiconductor companies despite strong performance, as concentration limits prevent further purchases.
cards.body:
A few artificial intelligence chip manufacturers have grown to dominate Asian stock market benchmarks, creating a structural challenge for investment funds that track regional indices. Companies including TSMC, Samsung, and SK Hynix have become so heavily weighted in major Asian stock indices that many funds have hit regulatory or internal limits on their holdings.

The concentration issue has forced active fund managers into a counterintuitive position of selling shares during rallies rather than adding to winning positions. Emerging markets funds are now seeking alternative investments as they cannot increase exposure to the dominant chip stocks. The situation has warped traditional stock-picking strategies across Asia, with the AI boom creating unexpected constraints for portfolio managers.

cards.headline: OpenEvidence applies artificial intelligence to help doctors with clinical decisions
cards.teaser: The fast-growing startup is using AI technology to assist physicians in finding answers to diagnostic and treatment questions.
cards.body:
OpenEvidence, a startup in the medical technology sector, is deploying artificial intelligence to support doctors in making clinical decisions. The company's platform helps physicians find answers to questions related to diagnosis and treatment by processing medical information.

The technology represents a growing trend of AI applications in healthcare settings, where speed and accuracy in accessing relevant medical knowledge can affect patient outcomes. The company has experienced rapid growth as healthcare providers seek tools to assist with the increasing complexity of medical decision-making. The platform aims to complement rather than replace physician judgment in clinical settings.

cards.headline: Marks & Spencer launches traineeship program for 1,000 young people
cards.teaser: The British retailer aims to address the growing number of young people not in employment, education, or training through a new initiative.
cards.body:
Marks & Spencer has launched a new traineeship program for 1,000 young people. The scheme is designed to address what the company identifies as a growing challenge: young people who are not in employment, education, or training.

The initiative combines practical work experience with structured learning to help participants develop job skills and move into permanent employment roles within the retail sector.

cards.headline: Astronomers identify source of repeating cosmic radio signals
cards.teaser: A student astronomer helped decode mysterious radio signals originating from an accreting white dwarf binary system.
cards.body:
Astronomers have identified the source of mysterious repeating radio signals from space, solving a puzzle that has intrigued researchers. The signals originate from an accreting white dwarf binary system, where matter from one star transfers to its companion. The discovery was published in Nature and involved contributions from a student astronomer.

The white dwarf system produces both periodic radio and X-ray emissions, creating a pattern that scientists describe as a Rosetta stone for understanding similar cosmic phenomena. Researchers from UNC-Chapel Hill helped crack the mystery by analyzing the signal characteristics and matching them to known stellar behaviors. The findings provide insight into how certain stellar systems generate electromagnetic radiation across multiple wavelengths.

cards.headline: Microsoft and Nvidia unveil new Windows PC designs powered by AI chips
cards.teaser: Microsoft showed its Surface Laptop Ultra at Computex while Nvidia announced the RTX Spark chip for personal AI computing.
cards.body:
Microsoft showcased the Surface Laptop Ultra at Computex, demonstrating its commitment to the premium PC hardware market. The device marks Microsoft's latest push to compete in the high-end laptop segment.

Nvidia introduced the RTX Spark chip, positioned as its most efficient PC processor to date, along with the N1x and N1 laptop chip specifications. Microsoft and Nvidia are collaborating to transform Windows PCs for an era of personal AI, creating hardware capable of running AI applications locally on devices rather than relying on cloud-based processing.

cards.headline: Apple prepares AI announcement at WWDC after two years of setbacks
cards.teaser: Apple's annual developer conference focuses on reviving Siri with new AI capabilities after stumbles in the AI race.
cards.body:
Apple is preparing to unveil new AI features at its Worldwide Developers Conference, with analysts saying the company needs a win after two years of struggling to compete in artificial intelligence. The announcements will include updates to Siri, iOS 27, macOS 27, and other software platforms. Wall Street is watching closely to see if Apple can catch up to competitors in the AI space.

Reports indicate that Apple will integrate Google's Gemini technology to power an improved version of Siri. The WWDC preview suggests Apple is getting a second chance at its AI rollout after previous efforts fell short of expectations. The company's developer conference will be streamed online, with major software announcements expected across its product lineup.

cards.headline: Samsung Galaxy S26 FE design revealed in early leak
cards.teaser: Images and regulatory filings show Samsung's upcoming affordable flagship phone with a redesigned camera layout.
cards.body:
The Samsung Galaxy S26 FE has appeared in hands-on images and regulatory database listings before its official announcement. The device features a new design compared to the Galaxy S25 FE, with an updated camera bump configuration. The WPC database listing confirms the phone will support Qi2 wireless charging.

The leaked images show what reviewers describe as a slightly funky camera arrangement that differs from previous Samsung designs. The Galaxy S26 FE represents Samsung's affordable flagship line, positioned below the main Galaxy S series in price while retaining many premium features. The early reveal provides a first look at design changes Samsung is making to distinguish this generation from its predecessor.

cards.headline: Gears of War: E-Day set for October console exclusive launch
cards.teaser: Microsoft announced the new Gears of War title will arrive on Xbox Series X/S and PC this fall.
cards.body:
Microsoft has confirmed that Gears of War: E-Day will remain exclusive to Xbox consoles and PC, ruling out a PlayStation 5 release. The announcement came during the Xbox Games Showcase, where the game was revealed as a major title in Microsoft's upcoming lineup.

The decision marks a shift in Microsoft's platform strategy, as the game had previously been rumored for a PS5 launch alongside its Xbox and PC releases. Gears of War: E-Day is scheduled to launch in October.

cards.headline: Atlus announces Persona 6 at Xbox Games Showcase
cards.teaser: The next mainline Persona game was officially revealed with graveyard visuals and a toxic green color scheme.
cards.body:
Atlus confirmed Persona 6 during the Xbox Games Showcase at Summer Game Fest 2026. The announcement came as a brief teaser, marking the long-awaited return of the Persona series following Persona 5.

The reveal showed the game's visual direction, featuring graveyard imagery and a toxic green aesthetic that represents a departure from previous entries in the franchise. This announcement was part of a strong year for Japanese RPG reveals at Summer Game Fest.

hero.headline: Jose Mourinho set to become Real Madrid head coach after Perez re-election
hero.teaser: Jose Mourinho is expected to be confirmed as Real Madrid's new head coach following Florentino Perez's re-election as club president.
hero.body:
Jose Mourinho is poised to be announced as Real Madrid's new head coach following Florentino Perez's successful re-election as club president until 2030.

Perez secured a decisive victory in Madrid's first competitive presidential election in 20 years, polling 65 percent of the vote. His challenger, 37-year-old Enrique Riquelme, received 35 percent support after a total of 33,555 club members participated in the ballot. The election results were initially delayed when Riquelme contested the validity of around 1,000 postal votes, though over 400 were subsequently disqualified.

Perez has served as Real Madrid president for 23 years across two separate spells, having first held the position between 2000 and 2006 before returning to the role in 2009. His re-election victory extends his tenure for another six years.

The confirmation of Mourinho's appointment is expected to be formally announced on Monday, with Madrid set to pay Benfica a 15 million euro release fee to secure the 63-year-old Portuguese coach. Mourinho will return to the Bernabéu for a second spell, more than a decade after his first stint at the club ended.

Mourinho joined Benfica last September but will now move on to one of European football's elite clubs. His appointment represents a significant move in the managerial landscape, particularly given his extensive pedigree managing top European sides including Chelsea and Manchester United.

The change at Madrid's helm comes as Perez also outlined ambitious plans for the club's future. The president has pledged to make a bid of at least 150 million euros on Tuesday for an unnamed "galactico" player, widely understood to be Michael Olise.

Perez's electoral victory means his vision for the club can proceed without the disruption of a change in presidency. His opponent had promised a notably different direction, proposing to appoint Raul Gonzalez Blanco as sporting director and attempting to recruit Jurgen Klopp as manager.

The stability provided by Perez's re-election through 2030 gives Real Madrid a clear leadership framework as the club moves into its next chapter. With Mourinho confirmed as the new head coach and significant investment planned for the squad, Madrid appears positioned to pursue an ambitious agenda in both domestic and European competition.

cards.headline: Christian Eriksen expected to leave hospital after collapse during Denmark match
cards.teaser: Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen is in good spirits and expected to be discharged from hospital following his on-field collapse against Ukraine.
cards.body:
Christian Eriksen collapsed on the pitch during Denmark's friendly match against Ukraine on Sunday in Odense. The midfielder, a former Tottenham and Manchester United player, held his chest in the 65th minute before losing consciousness. Medical staff quickly attended to him and the match was abandoned.

Denmark's team doctor Morten Boesen confirmed that Eriksen is in good spirits and doing well following the incident. The 34-year-old is expected to be discharged from hospital soon. This marks another serious health incident for Eriksen, who suffered cardiac arrest during a European Championship match in 2021.

cards.headline: Nelly Korda wins U.S. Women's Open for second consecutive major title
cards.teaser: Nelly Korda captured her first U.S.
cards.body:
Nelly Kord captured her first U.S. Women's Open title on Sunday, securing her second consecutive major championship. She finished one shot ahead of Charley Hull and Gaby Lopez, claiming a $2.5 million first prize. The victory came down to a dramatic final moment when Kord's 2½-foot par putt on the 18th hole curved around the cup before dropping in.

The win represents Kord's fourth major championship victory overall. She shot a steady two-under 69 in the final round to seal the triumph. Hull, competing in her bid for a first major title, and Lopez both fell just short of forcing a playoff.

cards.headline: Crusaders suffer record 134-0 defeat in rugby league
cards.teaser: The Crusaders endured the biggest defeat in the 131-year history of rugby league's top two divisions, losing 134-0.
cards.body:
The Crusaders have suffered the heaviest defeat in rugby league's 131-year history, losing 134-0. The scoreline represents the biggest margin of defeat ever recorded in the top two divisions of the sport.

This unprecedented result surpasses all previous records for lopsided matches at the highest level of professional rugby league competition.

cards.headline: Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett to report for mandatory minicamp
cards.teaser: Jacoby Brissett will report for Arizona's mandatory minicamp this week after holding out during the offseason program while seeking a contract adjustment.
cards.body:
Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett will report for the team's mandatory minicamp this week, ending his holdout from the offseason program. Brissett had been absent while negotiating a reworked contract for the upcoming season.

His attendance at the mandatory minicamp allows him to participate in required team activities as the Cardinals prepare for the new season.

cards.headline: Jude Bellingham faces competition for England starting spot at World Cup
cards.teaser: England manager Thomas Tuchel says Jude Bellingham will have to compete for a place in the starting lineup at the World Cup.
cards.body:
Jude Bellingham will have to compete for a starting position in England's midfield at the World Cup, according to manager Thomas Tuchel. The midfielder is not assured of a place in the first eleven and must earn his spot through performances.

Tuchel's stance indicates increased competition across England's squad as the team prepares for the tournament. Bellingham will need to prove himself rather than rely on his reputation or previous achievements to secure a starting role.

cards.headline: Knicks and Spurs prepare for Game 3 at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: The Knicks are working to maintain focus as Madison Square Garden hosts its first NBA Finals game since 1999 when they face the Spurs in Game 3.
cards.body:
Madison Square Garden will host its first NBA Finals game since June 25, 1999, as the Knicks face the Spurs in Game 3. The Knicks' winning streak has energized New York ahead of the historic matchup. Enhanced security measures are in place, with the NYPD canceling an outside watch party due to the high-profile nature of the event.

Despite trailing 2-0 in the series, the Spurs remain confident in their chances. Victor Wembanyama and his teammates are undaunted heading into Monday's game at the iconic arena.

hero.headline: Qween Jean Becomes First Openly Trans Person to Win Tony Award
hero.body:
Qween Jean made history at the Tony Awards when she won for Best Costume Design for the Broadway revival of Cats, becoming the first openly transgender person to receive the award. The win represents a significant milestone in the theater industry's recognition of trans artists working in technical roles.

Jean used her acceptance speech to reflect on broader social issues. "The world right now is deeply, deeply combating so many ailments, and we know as a society that when we come together, we can make real, permanent change," she said from the stage.

The Tony Awards ceremony celebrated excellence across multiple theater categories. John Lithgow and Lesley Manville led the list of individual winners, while a revival of Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman emerged as the evening's top winner, taking home six awards overall.

Jean's costume design work contributed to the visual storytelling of the Cats revival, which brought the enduring musical back to Broadway with updated production elements while preserving the theatrical framework that has sustained the show through decades of performances.

The achievement holds particular significance given the limited transgender representation in major entertainment awards. Jean's win provides visibility for trans artists working in costume design and other technical theater positions, areas where recognition has historically been scarce. The costume design category honors artists whose contributions shape how audiences visually experience stage productions, making Jean's recognition both a personal accomplishment and a moment of cultural importance for the broader theater community.

This win comes amid a complex national landscape surrounding transgender issues and representation in public life. Jean's presence at one of entertainment's most prestigious ceremonies signals a shift toward greater inclusion in award recognition, though transgender artists continue to remain underrepresented in major honors across the entertainment industry.

The Tony Awards, theater's highest honor, have recognized outstanding achievement in American musical and dramatic theater for decades. The ceremony showcases the year's most celebrated performances, productions, and creative contributions across numerous categories ranging from acting to design and technical work. Jean's historic win demonstrates the quality of work being produced by trans artists and highlights the continued importance of visibility and representation in spaces traditionally dominated by others.

Her achievement arrives at a moment when conversations about inclusion and diversity in entertainment remain central to industry discussions. By winning in a technical design category, Jean also underscores that transgender excellence spans all aspects of theatrical production, not only performance roles. This recognition may encourage future opportunities for trans artists in theater and related creative fields while acknowledging the exceptional work already being contributed by trans professionals throughout the industry.

cards.headline: Death of a Salesman Revival Wins Six Tony Awards
cards.teaser: The Arthur Miller revival led the night with six total awards including acting prizes for John Lithgow and Lesley Manville.
cards.body:
A revival of Arthur Miller's Death of a Salesman emerged as the biggest winner at the 79th Tony Awards, taking home six awards throughout the ceremony at Radio City Music Hall. The production received recognition across multiple categories including acting honors.

John Lithgow and Lesley Manville both won acting awards for their performances in the revival. The production brought Miller's classic American drama back to Broadway with a cast that earned widespread recognition from the theater community. Nathan Lane, also in the cast, did not win in his category despite expectations.

cards.headline: Schmigadoon! Wins Best Musical at Tony Awards
cards.teaser: The stage adaptation of the Apple TV+ series took home the top prize for Best Musical at the 79th Tony Awards.
cards.body:
Schmigadoon!, the Broadway musical based on the streaming television series, won Best Musical at the 2026 Tony Awards. The production defeated other new musicals in one of the ceremony's most anticipated categories.

The night's acting awards were distributed across multiple productions. Joshua Henry was among the performers recognized, alongside other winners from various shows including Death of a Salesman, which saw wins for John Lithgow and Lesley Manville.

cards.headline: Idris Elba Says James Bond Casting Rumors Were Never Real
cards.teaser: The actor addressed years of speculation about taking over the 007 role, saying audiences would not accept a Black actor in the part.
cards.body:
Idris Elba has dismissed longstanding speculation about playing James Bond, calling the rumors "never legit" and "not realistic." The 53-year-old actor stated that audiences would not accept a Black male actor in the iconic role.

Elba, who is known for playing heroic characters throughout his career, has faced persistent Bond casting suggestions since Daniel Craig's departure from the franchise in 2021. He currently stars in Masters of the Universe alongside Nicholas Galitzine.

cards.headline: Karlovy Vary Film Festival to Honor Maggie Gyllenhaal and Jesse Eisenberg
cards.teaser: The festival's 60th edition will recognize both actor-directors for their work in film.
cards.body:
The Karlovy Vary International Film Festival will honor Maggie Gyllenhaal and Jesse Eisenberg at its 60th edition, running July 3-11. Both Gyllenhaal and Eisenberg work as actors, directors, and screenwriters, with careers spanning performance and filmmaking.

Artistic director Karel Och said the two artists are distinguished by a certain trans-Atlantic sensitivity. Och noted that their work as actors and directors demonstrates an ability to bridge different filmmaking traditions. The festival recognition acknowledges their contributions to both acting and directing in contemporary cinema.

cards.headline: Samuel Releases Album Blending Latin and K-Pop Styles
cards.teaser: The international artist's new four-track album Samuelito merges Latin rhythm with Korean pop performance styles.
cards.body:
International artist Samuel released Samuelito, a four-track album combining Latin rhythm, reggaeton energy, and K-pop performance aesthetics. The project reflects his background working across multiple music industries and cultural contexts.

Born in Los Angeles to a Mexican family, Samuel developed his early career in the Korean music industry, where he built a performance style and vocal range across pop genres. The album represents his effort to merge the Latin musical traditions of his family background with the production and performance techniques he learned during his time in Korea.

cards.headline: Colony Holds Top Spot at South Korean Box Office
cards.teaser: The local action-horror thriller generated $4 million during its third weekend in theaters.
cards.body:
Colony maintained its lead at the South Korean box office during the June 5-7 weekend, earning $4 million from 603,868 admissions. The action-horror thriller captured a 44.35% revenue share in its third weekend, according to data from KOBIS, the Korean Film Council's tracking service.

Wild Sing launched during the same period, drawing strong audience numbers. The weekend demonstrated continued interest in South Korean films, with both releases performing well at the domestic box office.

hero.headline: Trump administration pursues equity stakes in AI companies
hero.body:
President Trump is seeking to have the U.S. government take ownership shares in major artificial intelligence companies, marking a significant departure from traditional Republican free-market principles. The administration justifies the approach as a way for taxpayers to profit from federal investments in the technology sector.

The equity-for-funding model has become a defining feature of Trump's second term economic policy. The U.S. government now holds shares in chipmakers, mining companies, and quantum computing firms, typically acquiring stakes when companies receive federal money that was originally allocated for other purposes. Trump recently commented that he "should be a stockbroker," referencing his administration's recent deal to take a stake in Intel.

This strategy represents a fundamental shift from Republican orthodoxy against government intervention in private markets. Traditional conservative economic policy opposes federal ownership of private companies and rejects the concept of government officials selecting which businesses to support through subsidies or equity investments. The approach has become anathema to free-market capitalism and Republican dogma about government picking winners and losers.

Trump's approach differs from similar proposals by progressive politicians in its stated motivation. Rather than pursuing equity stakes to redistribute corporate profits or exert public control over strategic industries, the administration presents the policy as a business transaction designed to generate returns for taxpayers. The president views the arrangements through the lens of dealmaking, seeking profit rather than advancing populist economic goals.

Companies like OpenAI and Anthropic may soon be worth trillions of dollars, making them attractive targets for government equity stakes. Trump has discussed deals "where the American people can benefit from the success of AI," according to public statements.

The policy raises significant questions about the federal government's long-term role in the private sector and whether the equity positions will generate the anticipated financial returns. The administration has not disclosed specific valuations of the government's current holdings or projections for future gains from its stakes in technology companies.

This shift in economic philosophy has already attracted criticism from different political perspectives. Some observers note the irony of a Republican administration embracing what resembles a "Bernie-like interest" in government ownership stakes, even as it distinguishes itself from progressive proposals through profit motivation rather than wealth redistribution or democratic control.

The extent to which the government will pursue these equity arrangements remains unclear. What is certain is that the equity-for-funding model has fundamentally altered how federal investments in strategic industries are being structured during Trump's second term, creating a hybrid approach that blends capitalist dealmaking with government ownership stakes.

cards.headline: Trump walks out of Meet the Press interview over election fraud questions
cards.teaser: The president ended an interview after being pressed on claims about the 2020 election and California primary results.
cards.body:
President Trump walked out of an NBC Meet the Press interview on Sunday after a tense exchange with host Kristen Welker. The interview, recorded Friday in Wisconsin, became contentious when Welker repeatedly challenged Trump's claims that the 2020 presidential election and California's recent primary elections were rigged.

Trump's abrupt exit came as the host pressed him on his false assertions about election integrity. The interview also touched on questions regarding compensation for those charged in the January 6 Capitol riot.

cards.headline: Congress fails to extend surveillance powers after Trump intelligence pick
cards.teaser: A bipartisan deal to reauthorize Section 702 spy powers collapsed following the president's nomination of Bill Pulte as intelligence director.
cards.body:
Negotiations for a long-term extension of Section 702 surveillance authorities broke down after President Trump selected Bill Pulte to lead the intelligence community. Congressional leaders had been working toward a bipartisan agreement on the spy powers legislation.

The Section 702 program allows intelligence agencies to monitor foreign communications. Pulte's nomination disrupted the legislative process that had appeared close to producing a compromise acceptable to both parties in Congress.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary
cards.teaser: Haaland, who served under President Biden, secured the Democratic nomination for governor and could become the first female Native American governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Haaland previously served as Secretary of the Interior in the Biden administration before entering the gubernatorial race.

If elected in the general election, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American to serve as a state governor. She will face the Republican nominee in the fall campaign.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary results
cards.teaser: Early returns show Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra ahead in the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra held leads in the California gubernatorial primary as vote counting continued. The contest features multiple candidates from both parties competing for their nominations to succeed Gavin Newsom.

Democratic candidates Katie Porter and Tom Steyer also sought their party's nomination, while Republican Chad Bianco competed alongside Hilton. California's primary system will determine which candidates advance to the general election.

cards.headline: Trump to attend NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: The president will become the first sitting president to attend the NBA Finals, despite expected protests from Knicks fans.
cards.body:
President Trump plans to attend Game 3 of the NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden, making him the first sitting president to attend the championship series. The New York Knicks are competing in the finals at their home arena.

Enhanced security measures are in place for the game. The Knicks are asking fans to arrive at least two hours before tipoff and to bring minimal belongings. The NYPD cancelled a watch party outside Madison Square Garden due to the president's attendance, following discussions between the Secret Service and police.

cards.headline: Children's wellbeing declined nationally since 2019
cards.teaser: A new report shows children in 29 states are faring worse than before the COVID pandemic, with implications for future economic growth.
cards.body:
Children's wellbeing declined nationally from 2019 to 2024, with kids in 29 states experiencing worse outcomes than pre-pandemic levels, according to a new report.

The decline has broader economic implications, as children's health, safety, education, and family stability directly influence their future workforce participation and economic productivity.
